solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Noble archbishop gutted in high-level cover-up?

parts.note: an earl is a nobleman

indicators.note: a gutted word has lost its insides, leaving only the outside letters of archbishop

explanation.surface: A scandal: some aristocratic churchman is caught concealing something at the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' leaves AP, the outside letters of 'archbishop'. The definition is playful: the ear sits high on the head, and this flap covers it.
explanation.definitionFit: A flap on a cap that covers the ear is a covering worn up on the head, hence a whimsical high-level cover.

clue.text: Lift English tax, in part to be returned

indicators.note: the English tax sits inside the other piece, shown by in
returned means the word for part is read backwards

parts.note: a part in a play is a role
VAT is value added tax, the UK sales tax

explanation.surface: Someone wants to lift an English tax, part of which is to be paid back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be returned' reverses the word for part, and 'in' puts English and tax inside it. 'Lift' looks like a verb but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Lift is the British word for the machine Americans call by this name, carrying people between floors.

clue.text: Cheerful jumbo heading off south of river

indicators.note: in a down entry, south of means placed below, so after
the head, or first letter, of the word for jumbo is taken away

parts.note: jumbo as an adjective means huge, giant

explanation.surface: An elephant happily trots off south of the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' removes G from GIANT to leave IANT; 'south of' puts it below R in this down entry. RIANT is a literary word for laughing or cheerful.
explanation.definitionFit: Riant is a literary adjective, borrowed from French, meaning smiling, laughing or merry.

clue.text: Left in a butt, almost getting free

indicators.note: in puts the abbreviation for left inside the other letters
almost drops the last letter of the word for butt

parts.note: a butt is something aimed at, a target

explanation.surface: Someone left inside a cask almost manages to get free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims TARGET to TARGE; 'in' places L inside A TARGE to give AT LARGE.
explanation.definitionFit: An escaped prisoner at large is roaming loose, not captured, so the phrase means free.

clue.text: Friend about to follow one who's easily manipulated

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for friend runs backwards

parts.note: a pal is a friend
to dog someone is to follow them closely

explanation.surface: A friend is about to follow someone who is a pushover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to follow' reads as one phrase in the surface but splits in two: 'about' is a reversal signal and 'to follow' is a verb synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who is a lapdog obeys a more powerful figure slavishly, like a pampered pet, so is easily controlled.

clue.text: A flexible-sounding plant?

indicators.note: sounding marks that the phrase is heard rather than spelt, giving a plant name

parts.note: a plus lissom, meaning supple or flexible

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about which plant might sound bendy.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'a lissom' (a supple) matches the flower name.
explanation.definitionFit: Alyssum is a low-growing garden flower of the cabbage family, often with small white blooms.

clue.text: Killer from ancient city hiding in endless wasteland

indicators.note: the city is concealed inside the shortened wasteland
endless drops the final letter of the word for wasteland

parts.note: a desert is a barren wasteland
Troy is the ancient city of the Trojan War

explanation.surface: A murderer comes out of a lost city buried in the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims the last letter of the wasteland, and 'hiding in' puts the ancient city inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: One who destroys or wrecks is a killer in a broad sense; the word is also used of a fast warship.

clue.text: After golf, wet snap may be so hard to define

definitions.text: snap may be so hard to define

indicators.note: after puts the word for wet behind the letter for golf

parts.note: G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
rainy weather is wet

explanation.surface: A golfer's photo taken in wet weather may come out blurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snap' is a photograph, not a break; a grainy photo has coarse visible specks and so lacks sharp outlines.
explanation.definitionFit: A photograph described as grainy has a coarse, speckled texture, so its details are fuzzy and hard to make out.

clue.text: Charles knocked around base labourer a long time ago

indicators.note: knocked around means the letters are battered into a new order

parts.note: e is the base of natural logarithms in mathematics

explanation.surface: Charles was roughed up by a worker at the base long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked around' rearranges CHARLES plus E. Heracles performed the Twelve Labours of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek hero is famous for his Twelve Labours, so he is the mythical labourer from antiquity.

clue.text: Hearty entertainment as Senate is organised outside hotel

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are placed around the letter for hotel
organised means the letters are put into a different order

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A rousing show is put on because the Senate is organised beyond the hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearty' is a sailor (a hearty, as in 'me hearties'), not an adjective. 'organised' rearranges AS SENATE IS around H.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearties are sailors, and their traditional work songs entertained them aboard ship.

clue.text: I'd agree no woman should be opposed

parts.note: the opposite of no is yes, the clue saying both words should be opposed
the opposite of woman is man

explanation.surface: Someone says they would agree that no woman should face opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should be opposed' applies to both 'no' and 'woman': swap each for its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: A sycophant who always concurs with the boss would say they'd agree, whatever is proposed.

clue.text: Flag from whiskey, getting behind

parts.note: W is whiskey in the NATO phonetic alphabet
aft means at the back of a ship, behind

explanation.surface: Someone flags after drinking whiskey and falling behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' looks like a verb meaning tire; here it is a noun, the nautical signal flag.
explanation.definitionFit: In naval use a waft is a flag or pennant hoisted as a signal, often knotted in the middle.

clue.text: Calming down clumsy Russian cutting what's on plate?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters cut into the registration abbreviation

parts.note: a car's number plate shows its registration, REG for short

indicators.note: clumsy means the letters of the word are awkwardly jumbled

explanation.surface: A clumsy Russian slicing food on a plate settles everyone's nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clumsy' rearranges the nationality and 'cutting' puts it inside the registration. The plate is a car's number plate, not crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: Comforting words that settle someone's fears are soothing, which is what calming someone down does.

clue.text: Stooping wife facing OTT malevolent spells?

parts.note: to be bent double is to stoop
over the top acting is hammy

explanation.surface: A hunched wife casts over-the-top evil spells.
explanation.walkthrough: A whammy is an evil curse, so two of them make a pair of malevolent spells; the question mark flags the play on the phrase's usual meaning of a twin setback.
explanation.definitionFit: A whammy is a jinx or curse; two together form a pair of evil spells, the literal reading of the phrase.

clue.text: Tormenting, as crossword compilers are supposed to

definitions.meaning: harassing persistently, as a fault or temptation that besieges someone

definitions.text: as crossword compilers are supposed to
definitions.meaning: compilers should ... puzzles, read as two words

explanation.surface: A wry dig that tormenting solvers is just what setters are meant to be doing.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitual sin that besieges a person torments them; split in two, the word also describes what setters ought to be doing.

clue.text: Lawless controller of estate, say?

parts.note: an estate is a type of car, and someone steering a stolen one recklessly for thrills is a lawless driver

explanation.surface: Sounds like a corrupt landowner running a country property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'estate' suggests land, but it is an estate car, the British term for a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who steals a car to drive it fast for fun is breaking the law while in control of the vehicle.

clue.text: Boy on back by you

indicators.note: on means the word for boy comes after the other pieces

parts.note: to second a motion is to back it
per means by, as in per post
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy rides piggyback beside you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' puts the boy last although he comes first in the clue; 'back' is the verb meaning support.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar, the pronoun used to address the listener is in the form after first, so you belongs to that category.

clue.text: Trick and get new fitting

parts.note: a con is a trick or swindle
to dig something is to get it, understand it

explanation.surface: Pull a trick and pick up something new to wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get' here means understand, the slang sense of dig.
explanation.definitionFit: Condign means deserved or appropriate, usually of punishment, so it is a formal word for fitting.

clue.text: Die without one's true love

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so the phrase for die surrounds the letter

parts.note: to pass on is to die
one gives the Roman numeral I, the 's read as has, a link

explanation.surface: A lover's lament: they would die without their one true love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking: the phrase for die is wrapped round the numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense romantic desire or ardour is the feeling at the heart of true love.

clue.text: Liquidised half of joint with sweet coating

indicators.note: the dessert word goes around the other piece like a coating

parts.note: pud is short for pudding, the British word for dessert or sweet

indicators.note: half of takes the first three letters of the word for a joint

parts.note: a reefer is a cannabis joint

explanation.surface: Half a joint of meat is blended and covered in a sweet glaze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' is a cannabis cigarette, not meat; 'half of' takes its first three letters and 'coating' wraps the dessert round them. 'Sweet' is the British word for dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has been pureed is mashed or blended until smooth and nearly liquid.

clue.text: Drinks in filthy place with dreadful urinals outside

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit outside the sty
dreadful means the letters are in a terrible mess

parts.note: a pigsty is a byword for filth

explanation.surface: Drinking in a dirty bar with horrid toilets outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadful' rearranges the toilets and 'outside' puts them round the filthy place. A rusty nail is a cocktail of Scotch and Drambuie.
explanation.definitionFit: The rusty nail is a cocktail of Scotch whisky and Drambuie, so a pair of them are drinks.

clue.text: Partly mark out round pods

indicators.note: round means the chosen letters are turned the other way
partly means only part of the words mark out are used

explanation.surface: Someone partly marks out some round pods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Partly' takes ARKO from 'mark out', and 'round' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Okra is a vegetable eaten as its green seed pods, also called ladies' fingers.

clue.text: Daisy steers very well, avoiding poles

indicators.note: poles are N and S, the north and south poles, which are left out

parts.note: steers are bullocks, oxen
very well, as reluctant agreement, means yes

explanation.surface: A daisy steers its course, keeping well clear of the poles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding poles' drops N from OXEN and S from YES.
explanation.definitionFit: The ox-eye is a common wild daisy with large white petals around a yellow centre.

clue.text: Old family doctor heading for Ipswich

parts.note: a medic is a doctor

indicators.note: heading for means the first letter of the town name

explanation.surface: An old family doctor sets off for Ipswich, a town in Suffolk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading for' looks like travel but takes I, the first letter of Ipswich.
explanation.definitionFit: The Medici were the powerful banking dynasty that ruled Renaissance Florence.

clue.text: Payments from advice in dispatches

indicators.note: in puts the advice inside the other word

parts.note: to dispatch is to send
a tip is a piece of advice

explanation.surface: Payments appear as advice in official dispatches from the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dispatches' is a verb here, SENDS, not military reports.
explanation.definitionFit: A stipend is a fixed regular salary or allowance, as paid to clergy, so stipends are payments.

clue.text: Butt boxer, say, that's close

parts.note: a boxer is a breed of dog
close as a noun means end

explanation.surface: A boxer butts an opponent at the close of the bout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxer' is the dog breed, not a fighter. A dog-end is British slang for a cigarette end.
explanation.definitionFit: Dog-end is British slang for the stub of a smoked cigarette, its butt.

clue.text: Make attractive as wear and tear do?

definitions.meaning: to win affection, make oneself liked
both words finish with the letters of the organ of hearing, so read as two words the answer says what they do

explanation.surface: Asks how something can be made appealing in the way that wear and tear affect it.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is cryptic: split the answer after three letters and it describes how the words 'wear' and 'tear' finish.
explanation.definitionFit: To win someone's affection, making a person loved or liked, is the everyday sense.
